construction: as e3-04, but the appended file's second record is an exact copy of replica C's last record (its footer)

scanner.reasoning: As e3-04, except that the first record read, the one before the last filemark, is a byte copy of C's footer. It parses (magic and CRC are this tape's), but its recorded footer position is 31 + 2N and it is read at 33 + 2N, so it supplies no layout. The rest is as e3-04: C's and B's footers are read one LBA before their recorded positions; A's layout plans EOD at 33 + 2N, before the tape's EOD at 35 + 2N, so it is not used. No footer supplies a layout, so no replica validates.
scanner.then: Returns BotStructuralRecoveryRequired, performs the Section 8.4.1 walk, and reports that terminal authority was not recovered.
quotes: A terminal replica's footer that parses supplies a planned layout only when its recorded footer position equals the position at which it was read, and the layout's planned EOD is at or after the tape's EOD.
A layout whose planned EOD lies before the tape's EOD may be followed by later tape files, so it is not used, and when no footer supplies a layout, no replica validates;
if no replica validates, perform the BOT structural recovery walk in Section 8.4.1.

If A, B, and C all fail, the Scanner returns an explicit `BotStructuralRecoveryRequired` outcome and performs the Section 8.4.1 walk; BOT Object classifications are likewise streamed before their terminal summary.
The walk does not invent a terminal replica. The Scanner MUST report that terminal authority was not recovered.

tape_files.1: Object candidate by elimination (item 7); identity unknown
tape_files.5: IndexSeparationExtent AB (item 3), damaged: measured N + 3 against planned N (TerminalIndexSeparationParse)
tape_files.6: IndexSeparationExtent BC (item 3); count agrees; one tape file and one LBA early. Damaged or intact: open
tape_files.7: TapeIndexReplica C (item 2); count agrees; one tape file and one LBA early. Damaged or intact: open
tape_files.8: readable foreign head, last record a copy of C's footer: OPEN, see open_points. Not a TapeIndexReplica by item 2's own terms, because its head is readable and carries no replica header magic; not a sidecar by item 6, because its last block is not a sidecar footer

walk.ends: EOD at the start of tape file 9
walk.object_identities: tape file 1: unknown; tape file 8, if admitted as an Object candidate, also unknown
open_points: Tape files 6 and 7: as in e3-04.

Tape file 8. Permitted: (a) Object candidate by elimination (item 7), identity unknown, outside the validated scope; (b) nonconformant trailing file, not admitted as an Object (Section 12.6); (c) weakest: damaged TapeIndexReplica, if Section 10.6's 'matching magic with malformed content is a typed control failure, never an Object' is read to cover a matching footer magic in a file whose readable head does not match. Item 2 gives the footer route only when the head is unreadable, which points away from (c). In every case the file is outside the validated scope, and the validation of files 0..3 is unaffected.
quotes: matching terminal-replica header magic commits the tape file to this control type. The header and measured block count are checked against the encoded component plan. A malformed frame or count mismatch is reported as a damaged terminal replica; it MUST NOT fall through to Object. When the head is unreadable, a matching, fully parsed terminal footer establishes the same type, after its measured count is checked.

the Scanner reads the file's last block. If it parses as a sidecar footer, the footer's total MUST equal the measured block count, and the Scanner verifies the tail header copy against the footer, field for field.
The last block it reads for that probe also serves the terminal footer probe of items 2 and 3.
The header and footer role magics match the tape; matching magic with malformed content is a typed control failure, never an Object.
Item 7 applies to a tape file that none of items 1 to 6 recognises.
A structural artifact after the exact terminal suffix is nonconformant and MUST NOT be admitted as an Object.

A map produced by the Section 8.4.1 walk, after the second pass of Section 12.3, is validated against the tape's final ParityMap when that ParityMap validates and is marked `is_final_directory`, and the map's canonical projection (Section 7.3) through the ParityMap's own entry hashes to its `canonical_map_digest`.
MUST treat rows beyond the validated prefix as forensic only, never as recovery inputs.
